title: Facebook leads — Oct 27, 2026 strong-eye review
summary_md:
A spare-usage day: the **4,800 newest unreviewed Facebook listings** (two runs of 2,400, Oct 22–27 sweeps within 50 miles of Keller) were screened by the strong model instead of the cheap one, every flag was identified from its photo, and **every lead below was judged against real eBay sold listings** pulled from eBay this afternoon — the sold comps are shown on each lead's page. 85 flags → 20 leads (Tier A 1, B 5, C 14); 65 killed at the comps step. Prices here are what the item is listed at; *pay up to* is the most that keeps $50+ profit at the conservative sold value.

**$0 / $1 listings are placeholders** — the seller wants an offer. Treat the pay-up-to figure as your ceiling and open lower.

Still unreviewed: ~14,000 older listings from these sweeps. Say *review the facebook posts* in any chat to run the next batch.
howto_md:
1. **Filter and sort** with the bar above the list. *Sort: recommended* = Tier A first, biggest margin first.
2. **Open a lead** for the sold comps (photo, price, date, link), the plain explainer, what to check at pickup, the first message to send, and the resale plan.
3. **Act the same day** — good local listings go within hours. Mark the status on the lead page (asked / offered / bought / passed) so the next review skips it.
4. Distances: ≤ 30 mi is a short-notice trip; 31–50 mi needs planning.
method_md:
- **Collected:** Refurbish Watcher sweeps Oct 22–27, 2026 (free, toys, entertainment, hobbies, antiques, jewelry, instruments, clothing, kids, home, books), 50-mile radius, ≤ $200.
- **Screened:** 4,800 listings on 100 contact sheets by Opus eye agents with the v3 Facebook brief (brand-name clothes/shoes/bags, books, toys, kids & kitchen, jewelry and inherent value; never cards/Funko/furniture/instruments/audio). 107 flags.
- **Identified (Stage A):** every flag's photo viewed at full size; 85 identified, 22 killed (replicas, dealer ads, misreads).
- **Sold comps (Stage B):** 170 eBay SOLD searches run in Dylan's Chrome on Oct 27; 1,346 sold listings with photos.
- **Judged (Stage C):** each flag's photo beside its sold comps; a lead needs ≥ 2 true matches (or a strong ID under $20, marked hunch), ≥ $50 profit at the conservative sold value, and ≥ 2× the ask above $50.
- Dylan's rules: Civic trunk/back-seat size, pickup ≤ 50 mi, no repairs, no authentication-dependent items.

name: 10K yellow gold tennis bracelet, ~30 g (melt value)
price_note: $390 is firm-sounding. At 30 g of 10K that's about $13 a gram, well below scrap. That only makes sense if the scale photo is real and the piece is solid gold, so verify before paying. (Older post from an earlier sweep; message to check it is still available.)
what: 10K gold is 41.7% pure, and a 30 g piece holds about 12.5 g of pure gold. Pawn shops and refiners buy it by weight, and on eBay 10K tennis bracelets sell for about $45-50 a gram. Treat the clear stones as worthless.
evidence: 10K tennis bracelets sold Oct 2026 at about $45-52 a gram: 6.3 g for $300 (#2), 6.7 g for $350 (#3), 3.7 g for $185 (#6), and 6.99 g for $325 (#1). At 30 g that's $1,300+ before fees, or roughly $1,000+ at a pawn or refiner payout.
resale: Scrap or pawn payout for quick cash, or eBay as a 10K tennis bracelet with the weight in the title.

plan.title: 10K Yellow Gold Tennis Bracelet 30 Grams Solid Gold Stamped 10K

checks: Meet at a pawn shop or jeweler and have it acid- or XRF-tested and weighed on their scale before paying
10K or 417 stamp on the clasp
Scale reads 30.0 g, not 3.0 g, with the scale tared and the bracelet alone on it
Not magnetic, and no brass or green showing at worn edges
Solid links, not hollow
message: Hi! Is the 10K bracelet still available? Is it stamped 10K on the clasp? Would you be OK meeting at a jewelry or pawn shop in Grapevine so we can weigh it together?
risks: It's plated, or the real weight is far below 30 g. Dylan has no test kit, so never pay without a shop test.

price_note: $1 is a placeholder. The title says 'Pristine' and 'Fine/Near Fine', so the seller knows what these are and the real ask will probably be in the hundreds. Get the number before driving 31 miles. (Older post from an earlier sweep; message to check it is still available.)
what: Franklin Library and Easton Press made full-leather, gilt-edged classics for collectors from the 1970s to the 2000s. Collectors and decorators buy them in small themed lots, at about $10-25 a volume for common titles and more for signed first editions or the Shakespeare set.
evidence: Franklin leather lots sold Oct 24-26, 2026: 11 books $130 (#2), 5 books $100 (#3, #5, #6), 5 books $70 (#7). That works out to roughly $12-20 a volume before fees. 127 volumes at a conservative ~$8-10 net each is about $1,000.
resale: eBay in themed lots of 5-10 (Pulitzer, 100 Greatest, Greek and Roman, Shakespeare), with any signed first editions listed on their own. Selling the whole library to a local collector or a book dealer is the quick exit.

plan.title: Franklin Library Lot of 5 Leather Bound Gilt Edge Books 100 Greatest Masterpieces Fine

checks: Title page or spine says Franklin Library or Easton Press (not Barnes & Noble leatherette or Heritage)
Count the volumes and photograph the spines so you can pick out signed or limited first editions and the Shakespeare set

Gilt page edges bright and silk ribbon markers present
Confirm how many boxes there are and that it all fits in the Civic in one or two trips
message: Hi! I'm interested in your Franklin Library and Easton Press collection. What's your actual asking price for the whole lot, and are any of them signed first editions?
risks: The real ask comes in near retail. It also takes a lot of time and listings to turn 127 books into cash, and damaged or common titles will drag the per-volume price down.

price_note: $20 for the albums; the seller may not have priced in whatever coins are inside - or they may be empty. (Older post from an earlier sweep; message to check it is still available.)
what: Navy Whitman-style coin folders for Franklin halves, Anthony dollars and a US silver series. Every Franklin half is 90% silver, so even a partly filled album is worth far more than $20; an empty one is worth ~$10.
evidence: Complete 35-coin Franklin albums sold Oct 2026 for $700-950 (#1,#2,#3,#4,#6,#7,#8); a 13-coin partial sold for $355 (#5) - roughly $15-25 per coin.
resale: eBay (sell Franklin album as a set or partial; silver eagles individually) or a local coin shop for a quick cash-out.

plan.title: Franklin Half Dollar Whitman Album 1948-1963 90% Silver - [N] Coins

checks: Open every album and count the coins - if empty, pass or pay ~$10
Franklins should be dated 1948-1963 and look silvery, not copper-edged
Non-magnetic and correct weight (Franklin ~12.5 g) - rules out replicas
Silver Eagle (if any) reads '1 OZ. FINE SILVER'
Note empty holes and key dates (1948, 1949-S, 1953)
message: Hi! Are there coins in the albums, or are they empty? Roughly how many in the Franklin half dollar book?
offer_plan: Pay the $20 if coins are in them; walk away above $50 unless the Franklin album is mostly full.
risks: Albums are empty (most 'coin books' listings are) - confirm by message before the 68-mile round trip; also pulled/replica coins.

what: A lot of at least four boxed designer men's colognes: Polo Red Rush 4.2oz, Polo Blue, Polo Red and Coach for Men EDT. Boxed full-size designer fragrance sells steadily on eBay to buyers looking for below-retail bottles.

checks: Cellophane tight and factory-folded, no glue gaps or loose wrap
Batch code on box bottom matches code on bottle base
Boxes not marked tester; bottles full, sprayer crisp, juice color correct (Red Rush pale red, Blue blue)

message: Hi! Are the colognes still available? What are you asking for the lot, and are they all sealed/full?

name: Snap-on cordless tool and work light lot (CT8810-series 18V impacts, Snap-on lights, hand tools)
price_note: $0 is a placeholder; the real price must be asked. The chest itself won't fit a Civic, so this only works for the contents.
what: A Snap-on top chest stocked with Snap-on red cordless tools, work lights, hammers and pliers. Mechanics buy used Snap-on tools on eBay because new ones cost several times more off the truck.
evidence: Bare Snap-on CT8810 3/8in 18V impacts sold 4x Oct 21-26, 2026 for $60-85 (#1,#3,#4,#6); exact tool models in the lot are not readable in the photo, so value assumes only ~2 impacts plus lights.
resale: eBay, each power tool separately; hand tools as a small lot

Look for engraved names/IDs or ground-off markings (stolen tool risk)

price_note: $65 firm ask; only works if the bag is ~2 lb or more of genuine minifig parts.
what: A large bag of LEGO minifigure parts and accessories. Minifig parts sell for far more per pound than plain bricks because builders use them to complete figures.
evidence: 1 lb random minifig lot sold $125 Oct 26 (#2); 1/16 lb minifig part lots sold ~$19 (#4,#7). A ~2 lb bag sold whole nets ~$135 after fees.

Mostly minifig parts, not plain bricks

message: Hi! Is the minifig bag still available? About how much does it weigh, and is it all genuine LEGO?

name: Nike SB Dunk Low Ben & Jerry's 'Chunky Dunky' (CU3244-100)
price_note: $0 is a placeholder. A seller with a real pair will probably want a few hundred dollars. The real price and size have to be asked, and I assumed about $20 only to pass the screen.
what: A 2020 Nike SB collaboration with Ben & Jerry's, with cow-print hair, a dripping yellow swoosh and tie-dye lining. It is one of the most sought-after Dunks of recent years, so sneaker collectors pay hundreds even for worn pairs. It is also one of the most counterfeited.
evidence: 4 likely-authentic pairs sold Oct 20-26, 2026 for $550-899 (#1,#2,#5,#7). Two at $208-239 (#3,#4) are questionable, and two at $70 (#6,#8) are fakes ('Custom KO'). This shows how big the fake market is.
resale: eBay with Authenticity Guarantee (sneakers over $150 get authenticated free), or GOAT

plan.title: Nike SB Dunk Low Ben & Jerry's Chunky Dunky CU3244-100 Size __ Used

checks: Inside tag reads CU3244-100 with a matching size and production dates, and the box label matches it
Cow print is real pony hair with texture you can feel, not flat printed fabric
Swoosh is a mustard-yellow 'melting' drip shape with clean edges, and the outsole is green with an ice-cream drip pattern
Insoles have the Chunky Dunky graphics, and the lining is tie-dye
No glue mess or crooked stitching; if anything feels off, walk away (eBay authentication will reject a fake)
message: Hi! Are the Chunky Dunky SBs still available? What size are they, and what are you asking? Do you still have the original box?
risks: Fakes are everywhere, and Dylan can't authenticate sneakers himself. A fake is a total loss, because eBay authentication will reject it. Also, the seller's real price may be close to market.

name: Special-edition sprayed-edge hardcovers (Fairyloot/Owlcrate/Illumicrate style), ~30-35 book lot
price_note: $10 is almost certainly per book, not for the shelf. At $10 each this loses money; it only works if she'll take a bulk price for the whole lot (~$200 or less) or lets you pick the best titles.
what: Subscription-box special editions of YA and romantasy novels with sprayed or printed page edges, made in limited runs. Booktok readers and collectors buy them used, especially signed copies and popular series.
evidence: Six sold lots Aug-Oct 2026 work out to roughly $7-22 per book: 3 for $37 (#1), 6 for $45 (#2), 4 for $86 (#5), a mixed lot for $161 (#6), 8 for $117.50 (#8).
resale: eBay in lots of 4-8 by series or box (Fairyloot, Owlcrate); signed copies listed singly. Facebook local book groups for the rest.

plan.title: Special Edition Book Lot Sprayed Edges Fairyloot Owlcrate Illumicrate Romantasy Hardcover
plan.price: $120 per lot of 8, or best offer

checks: Confirm the price: per book or for the whole shelf
Look for Fairyloot / Owlcrate / Illumicrate marks on endpapers or copyright page, and any signatures
Sprayed edges bright, no fading, scuffs or water marks
Count the books and note duplicates or plain retail editions mixed in
message: Hi! Are the special edition books $10 each, or would you take an offer for both shelves together? Are any of them signed?
offer_plan: Open at $150 for everything, walk away above $220.
risks: Price is per book and she won't bulk-discount; several are plain retail hardcovers rather than box editions; slow sale in small lots with heavy shipping. 46mi drive.

title: Lego collection garage sale

comps.t: LEGO Icons: Concorde (10318) Complete Set w/ Display Stand
LEGO Icons Concorde Airbus 10318

name: LEGO Icons Concorde 10318 (built) plus Technic sets
price_note: $1 is a placeholder for a garage-sale listing; sets are almost certainly priced individually at the sale. Real per-set prices must be asked before driving out.
what: A garage-sale table of built LEGO sets; the white Concorde (Icons 10318, 2,083 pieces) is clearly visible, along with what look like a Technic Mack Anthem semi, a Technic heavy-duty tow truck and Technic F1 cars. Adult LEGO collectors buy built sets complete and dust-free, and the Concorde is a retired-style display piece that still sells steadily.
evidence: Built/used Concorde 10318 sold Oct 23, 2026 for $75 twice (#3 complete with display stand, #4). The $117-$199 comps (#1,#2,#5,#6,#8) are boxed/new and do not match a loose built model; #7 is just a wall mount. No comps were pulled for the Technic sets, so their value is unproven upside.
resale: Facebook Marketplace local pickup for the built Concorde (avoids shipping a fragile 2,000-piece model); eBay only if broken down and bagged with instructions.

plan.title: LEGO Icons Concorde 10318 - Built, Complete, Display Ready

checks: Ask if the Concorde is complete - nose, landing gear and display stand all present
Ask for instructions and box (adds value; missing box is fine for local sale)
Confirm real LEGO - 'LEGO' stamped on studs
Check for sun yellowing on the white pieces and broken/missing parts on the Technic sets
Get individual prices for the Mack Anthem 42078 and Tow Truck 42128 before deciding on more than the Concorde
message: Hi! Interested in the LEGO sets from your garage sale. What are you asking for the Concorde, and is it complete with the stand? Also what would you take for the big Technic semi and tow truck?
offer_plan: Open at $15 for the Concorde, walk away above $20 unless the Technic sets come bundled cheap.
risks: The $1 is fake - real asks are likely $50+ per set, which kills the margin; built Concorde only proved $75 sold, and it is fragile to transport.
